title: Multi-parameter assessment of thrombus formation on microspotted arrays of thrombogenic surfaces
protocol: Degrease new coverslips with 2 M HCl in 50% ethanol.
Wash coverslips twice with milliQ water.
Leave coverslips to dry on a drying rack.
Prepare coating material at 50-250 μg/mL as described.
Mount coverslip onto precision mall for coating.
Apply 0.5 µL of coating solution in the assigned place and remove from the mall.
Store coverslip in humid environment for 60 minutes at room temperature to allow coating material to bind.
Block uncoated glass with blocking buffer.
Leave blocked coverslip in humid environment for 30 minutes.
Wash blocked coverslip with saline.
If not immediately used, store coverslip in humid environment.
Connect tubing to inlet and outlet of the flow chamber.
Rinse chamber and tubing with flow buffer.
Check for absence of air bubbles in the chamber and tubing.
Mount coated coverslip on top of the chamber.
Place chamber with coverslip in aluminium holder.
Tighten screws securely.
Check that flow chamber system is leak-tight by perfusion with flow buffer.
Flush out any bubbles in the chamber thoroughly.
Add 0.5 mL saline into a 5 mL polystyrene blood collection tube.
Add 40 U/mL fragmin to the collection tube.
Add 40 µM PPACK just before venipuncture.
Draw blood according to local protocols.
Mix blood directly with anticoagulant solution.
Incubate the collected blood at 37°C for 10-15 minutes.
Add additional 20 µM PPACK once per hour.
Only for experiments to determine stable platelet adhesion or thrombus volume, add 0.5 µg/mL DiOC6 to 0.5 mL blood sample.
Allow staining of the blood cells for 5 minutes.
Draw 0.5 mL blood sample into 1 mL syringe equipped with blunt needle.
Connect syringe with blood sample to inlet tubing of prepared flow chamber.
Carefully avoid air bubbles in the connection.
Prepare a 1 mL syringe with flow buffer containing required fluorescent labels.
Mount the flow chamber and holder on the stage of the microscope.
Identify the position of microspots using a camera.
Focus on the optical plane of one microspot.
Place a syringe filled with whole blood on the perfusion pump in push mode.
Ensure proper pump settings for arterial or venous wall shear rates.
Switch the pump on when the blood reaches the site of the microspots.
Rinse shortly to prevent disaggregation of thrombi during the experiment.
Record DiOC6 fluorescence microscopic images at 2-second intervals for the first 2 minutes.
Change the syringe containing blood with a syringe containing flow buffer after 3.5, 4 or 6 minutes of perfusion as appropriate.
Set the pump rate to 1000 s^-1^ when changing syringes.
Rinse chamber with flow buffer for 2 minutes.
Take confocal z-stacks from thrombi during stasis; capture 2 to 3 stacks per microspot.
Rinse shortly to prevent disaggregation of thrombi.
Prevent air bubbles in flow chamber during syringe replacements.
Change syringe containing blood with a syringe containing fluorescent labels; set pump rate at 1000 s-1.
Perfuse buffer with labels through the flow chamber for 2 minutes; leave 1 minute for staining.
Take brightfield microscopic images (5 per microspot) under flow during perfusion.
Change syringe containing labels by syringe with flow buffer; and perfuse for 2 minutes to remove unbound label.
Take fluorescence images during stasis (5 images per microspot).
Determine morphological score of thrombi on coverslip based on recorded brightfield phase-contrast or DIC images.
Score at a 5-point scale.
Threshold every image within one time series with the same threshold → binary image.
Choose the first binary image as “source image 1” and the second binary image as “source image 2”.
Click “subtract” with constant values at “0”.
Repeat steps for the next images.
Choose “measure” → “integrated morphometry analysis”.
Measure all binary images and subtracted images.
Export all values to Excel spreadsheet, and calculate % of change between consecutive images.
Use edge detection in both horizontal and vertical directions for each image.
Use the horizontally filtered image for threshold setting → binary image.
Apply morphological close filter (diamond, width = 12) and open filter (circle, diameter = 5).
Transfer regions to brightfield/fluorescence image and check region detection.
Export data to Excel file and convert pixel numbers to % surface-area-coverage.
Filter images using morphological bottom hat filter (diamond, width = 15), then close filter (diamond, width = 4).
Threshold closed image → binary image.
Apply morphological dilate filter (square, width = 2).
Transfer regions to original image and check region detection.
Export data to Excel file and convert pixel numbers to % surface-area-coverage.
Rank individual features from small to large in an Excel file.
Exclude all features smaller than the size of one single platelet (≈ 100 pixels).
Integrate the values of the features by calculating the accumulated sum of pixels.
Convert pixel size into µm².
Divide the accumulated feature size by the total accumulated sum of all feature sizes, and express as a percentage.
Calculate the area above the percentage curve in µm².
Express results on a logarithmic scale.
Use scrap filter with minArea: 1 and maxArea: 100.
Apply separation filter with count: 3 and in Morphology mode.
Transfer regions to original image for verification of region detection accuracy.
Export data to an Excel file.
Convert pixel numbers to µm³.
